tested_scope.composition: mutable fixed-name Git ref R + content-addressed immutable object O + role-local selector S
tested_scope.two_factor_rule: accept only when the discoverable ref target SHA equals the exact immutable object SHA expected by the current selector; generation labels inside the object are not identity
scenarios: ref recreated to the same old immutable object
ref recreated to a different immutable object with copied generation fields
main/selector rewind loses the expected-object digest
candidate_variants: R target plus current selector expected SHA
R target plus copied generation fields without exact expected SHA
R plus a second mutable same-repository ref to the same immutable object
R target plus SHA deterministically derived from a current irreversible-effect identity
fail closed whenever the exact expected SHA is absent
tested_scope.scope_guard: bounded logical mechanism matrix derived from the source-qualified Part79 Git ref/tag model; not a production failure-rate estimate

ref_plus_current_expected_sha.recreate_same_old_object: rejects only while current S still expects a newer SHA; if S is rewound with the rollback domain, old R+old expected SHA is an ABA-indistinguishable historical-valid pair
ref_plus_current_expected_sha.recreate_different_object_copied_generat: rejects when S retains the exact expected SHA because immutable identity differs even if fields are copied
ref_plus_current_expected_sha.selector_rewind_loses_expected_sha: cannot complete the two-factor check; safe behavior is fail_closed
ref_plus_current_expected_sha.stateless_reconstruction: works only if a current non-rollback source still supplies the expected SHA

ref_plus_generation_fields_only.recreate_same_old_object: unsafe if old generation fields remain syntactically valid
ref_plus_generation_fields_only.recreate_different_object_copied_generat: unsafe because copied labels do not bind immutable identity
ref_plus_generation_fields_only.selector_rewind_loses_expected_sha: appears available but has no non-reusable identity proof

two_mutable_refs_plus_immutable_object.recreate_same_old_object: both names can be recreated to the same old target within the same rollback/reuse authority domain
two_mutable_refs_plus_immutable_object.recreate_different_object_copied_generat: exact common target identity detects disagreement but does not prove current incarnation after coordinated recreation
two_mutable_refs_plus_immutable_object.stateless_reconstruction: discovers an object but cannot distinguish coordinated ABA from a never-advanced history

effect_derived_expected_sha.recreate_same_old_object: safe only if the derivation input is itself current, non-reusable and survives the rollback domain
effect_derived_expected_sha.recreate_different_object_copied_generat: exact derivation rejects a different SHA
effect_derived_expected_sha.selector_rewind_loses_expected_sha: can recover only when the effect identity remains independently discoverable
effect_derived_expected_sha.stateless_reconstruction: narrowly viable only when an already-unavoidable authoritative effect domain exposes durable current idempotency/status; using a new hosted authority solely as witness is rejected
effect_derived_expected_sha.acceptance_blocker: generic recurring-Chat mechanism cannot assume a rollback-surviving effect identity outside the role-local repository domain without reintroducing an external authority dependency

fail_closed_without_expected_sha.recreate_same_old_object: safe by refusal when freshness cannot be proven
fail_closed_without_expected_sha.stateless_reconstruction: does not reproduce useful progress; remains unresolved

result.new_falsification: A mutable discoverability anchor plus immutable content identity is not a rollback-surviving two-factor freshness proof when the exact expected immutable identity is stored only inside the same rollback domain. Exact SHA comparison defeats substitution and copied-generation attacks while the expectation survives, but coordinated rollback/recreation to an old historically valid pair remains ABA-indistinguishable.
result.narrow_effect_identity_result: Deriving the expected object SHA from an irreversible-effect identity helps only if that identity itself is current, non-reusable, independently discoverable and rollback-surviving. If it is stored in the same selector domain, nothing is gained; if supplied by a new hosted witness service, the zero-external-coordination acceptance boundary is violated.

public_sources.qualified_claim: Git refs are mutable named handles that can be created, updated and deleted/recreated.
Annotated tag object identity is distinct from the mutable refs/tags name, separating immutable object identity from discoverability.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.unresolved_child: find a rollback-surviving statelessly discoverable freshness witness whose current non-reusable identity cannot be jointly rewound or recreated with the role-local selector, without adding a hosted authority, finite quota, richer-mode arbitration or user execution

continuation: Part81: execute exactly one bounded same-authority impossibility leaf. Construct paired histories H0 (generation g remains current forever) and H1 (advance to g+1, publish irreversible effect, then rollback every role-local discoverability pointer/ref/selector to the exact H0-observable state). Test whether any stateless scheduled-Chat decision procedure restricted to current role-local repository observations can distinguish H0 from H1. If observational equivalence holds, record the minimal extra assumption needed to break it, then test only zero-cost quota-independent assumptions already inside the unavoidable authoritative effect domain; do not introduce a new hosted witness service.
